answer: A mirror shows only what stands before it, so standing must be reflected twice. An identity needs two holders outside its own harbor to countersign its mirror entry, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses instead of one clique. Each entry is priced by rank: the k-th entry an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still requiring unrelated guarantors. A plume audit replays a random entry each epoch, and an unconfirmed entry voids the whole harbor. Sealed records cannot be pooled, lent, or re-dated.
